title: Analysis of epiretinal membranes
summary: Epiretinal proliferations and membranes lead to very different consequences for the eye, depending on the cause. While so-called idiopathic glioses lead to distortion and deterioration of vision, in proliferative vitreoretinopathy the membranes lead to retinal detachment with considerable consequences. We want to understand whether both types of these membranes differ in their biochemical status and whether this could result in a possible therapeutic approach.

interventions.name:
15 patients with idiopathic epiretinal membranes
Only the preoperative situation was described: History, visual acuity, eye pressure, slitlamp findings, funduscopy, OCT-imaging

15 patients with PVR membranes after retinal detachment
Only the preoperative situation was described: History, visual acuity, eye pressure, slitlamp findings, funduscopy, OCT-imaging

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing surgery to remove an epiretinal membrane. Group I: for idiopathic epiretinal gliosis. Group II: for proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
Exclusion criteria:
age < 18, severe systemic diseases
